A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sparsity–quantization study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression experiments on OPT, LLaMA and ViT, alongside seed robustness, layer-error and synthetic-block analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds GPTQ, ResNet-50, downstream-task and additional compression-control experiments.

M1.justification: The analyzed compression operations and principal recipes remain unchanged: sparse fine-tuning followed by quantization versus quantized-and-sparse fine-tuning. GPTQ experiments evaluate an existing alternative; expanded implementation disclosures do not establish a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Alongside retained WikiText2 and ImageNet evaluations, v2 adds PTB and C4 perplexity evaluations in Table 11 and zero-shot ARC-c, ARC-e, HellaSWAG and WinoGrande evaluations in Tables 15–16. This substantially expands represented language data and task requirements.

E2.justification: Appendix N newly evaluates GPTQ-4b in compression-order comparisons with magnitude pruning and SparseGPT, including compression-only controls in Table 10. Existing comparison methods in Tables 1–2 and v1 Table 6/v2 Table 7 are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds selected-layer experiments without fine-tuning, isolated-layer quantization, checkpoint comparisons, and ResNet-50/additional OPT configurations. The retained cumulative-error experiment changes from HBFP8 and mean error in v1 Figure 1 to HBFP6 and L2 error in v2 Figure 1. Section 4 also explicitly excludes the LLM head from compression; these reported changes do not establish reruns of retained benchmark tables.

E4.justification: New analyses examine single-layer error persistence (Appendix I), compression without fine-tuning (P), quantization collisions (Q), and checkpoint/master-weight behavior during fine-tuning (S). The cumulative layer-error study already existed in v1 Appendix G and is revised and moved to Section 4.3, rather than being wholly new.

E5.justification: Appendix H retains the same three-seed means and standard deviations for OPT-125M with HBFP8/6, renumbered from Table 8 to Table 9. The additional experiments introduce no expanded repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 10–17 and new figures add substantial results, while Tables 1–2 retain their original scores. For example, Table 10 newly reports perplexities of 30.93 versus 35.59 for S->Q versus Q->S with GPTQ and 50% sparsity on selected OPT-125M layers. Figure 1 is replaced under different quantization and error-measurement settings, so its values are not directly comparable across versions.

T1.justification: Appendix J adds Theorem J.2 directly comparing L1 composition errors, an intended general-norm bound in J.1, and expanded Lp attainability arguments. Definition 3.9 newly formalizes dot-product orthogonality using strict inequality. These exceed proof relocation, although J.1 introduces inconsistent quantization-versus-error notation.

C1.justification: The central claims of non-orthogonality and the preferred S->Q order remain. The introduction replaces the headline penalty of up to 7.96 perplexity points from suboptimal ordering with up to 13% additional perplexity error even under optimal ordering; the abstract and conclusion also expand their stated empirical support to CNNs.

C2.justification: v2 adds arguments connecting fixed-weight theory to fine-tuning through master-weight and checkpoint analyses, explains why unrestricted pruning without retraining obscures ordering effects, and explicitly excludes GPTQ/second-order methods from its theoretical coverage. The earlier detailed error-term interpretation largely moves to Appendix M.

D1.justification: Table 6 and Appendix S newly document FP32 master weights and optimizer updates, compressed attention matrix multiplications, and quantization during backward passes. Section 4 identifies the LLMs as base models. Existing hyperparameter tables, hardware, runtimes and the code/data access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 now explicitly acknowledges previous studies testing both compression orders, adding works such as Wang et al. (2022), Zandonati et al. (2023) and Park et al. (2019). GPTQ, OWQ and references supporting new evaluations are also added. This refines positioning while retaining the central gap concerning mathematical understanding.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and related-work narrative are substantially rewritten. Proofs move from Section 3 into Appendix J, cumulative layer analysis moves into Section 4.3, and detailed error interpretation moves into Appendix M. Terminology changes throughout from orthogonality bound to orthogonality threshold.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6 and 10–17 and Figures 2 and 7–11, redraws and relocates Figure 1, and incorporates sparse-versus-dense differences into retained result tables. The conference layout, removal of appendix line numbers and substantially denser tables further change presentation.

improvement.justification: The added experiments without fine-tuning, checkpoint controls and downstream/GPTQ evaluations strengthen empirical support, while new implementation disclosures improve reproducibility. However, Definition 3.9 introduces strict inequality inconsistent with the stated no-additional-error criterion, and J.1 introduces quantization/error notation inconsistencies absent from v1's corresponding proof. These regressions in the central mathematical exposition offset part of the validation gains, leaving a limited net improvement.
